summary: Check that the ICS justifies every recommendation declared not applicable or not met.

units.note: Review justifications recorded in the ICS.

rationale: Unit a reviews SO-supplied ICS only.
group_note: Whole group is ICS review; nothing passive.

summary: Assess from IXIT whether non-user-defined passwords used outside factory default are generated unique per device.

units.note: Judge documented password generation for per-device uniqueness.

rationale: Unit a is IXIT review; per-device uniqueness cannot be judged from one device's traffic.
outside_procedure_cues: A cleartext credential matching a public default-password list would hint at universal defaults; the conceptual case reviews only IXIT.
group_note: Uniqueness per device and IXIT completeness need SO data; conceptual part impossible.

summary: Look for undocumented password mechanisms, check user-defined passwords are enforced, and check generated passwords match the documented mechanism.

units.note: Find password logins reachable on network or in manual, compare to IXIT.
Operate setup to see user must set password.
Compare real device passwords with documented generation.

rationale: Verdict compares discovered mechanisms and password generation with the IXIT (a, c) and needs setup interaction (b); per v2.1 not reachable passively.
outside_procedure_cues: Cleartext HTTP Basic, Telnet or MQTT logins and answering login services reveal password mechanisms; IXIT completeness cannot be judged.
group_note: Uniqueness per device and IXIT completeness need SO data; conceptual part impossible.

summary: Judge whether the documented generation of pre-installed passwords avoids regularities, common strings, links to public data, and low complexity.

units.note: Check documented generator for obvious regularities.
Check for dictionary strings or common patterns.
Check relation to public data like MAC or SSID.

rationale: Substitution: a pre-installed password seen in cleartext can be checked against the MAC/SSID (b, c) and the dictionary named by the TS; FAIL only, PASS needs the IXIT mechanism.
assumptions: observed cleartext password is the pre-installed one
one observed password reflects the generation mechanism
group_note: Generation-mechanism quality (conceptual) impossible; only cleartext-exposed passwords give indications.

summary: Check that actual pre-installed passwords plausibly follow the documented generation mechanism.

units.note: Compare real pre-installed passwords against documented format.

rationale: Verdict is deviation from the IXIT generation description (unit a); per v2.1 assuming IXIT content is not allowed.
outside_procedure_cues: Pre-installed passwords sent in cleartext can be seen and checked for form; the property route is 5.1-2-1.
group_note: Generation-mechanism quality (conceptual) impossible; only cleartext-exposed passwords give indications.

summary: Determine from IXIT whether any machine-to-machine authentication relies on passwords.

units.note: Inspect documented authentication factor of M2M mechanisms.

rationale: Substitution: a cleartext M2M login carrying a password (e.g. MQTT CONNECT) shows passwords in use (unit a); PASS would need all M2M channels visible.
assumptions: observed credential exchange is M2M login with a password
observed channels cover the M2M mechanisms the IXIT would list
group_note: Only cleartext M2M logins observable; encrypted M2M authentication and IXIT review impossible.

summary: Search for undocumented mechanisms and check whether M2M authentication accepts passwords.

units.note: Check if M2M login accepts passwords; examples are MITM and mode changes.

rationale: Unit b: a cleartext M2M login with password (e.g. MQTT CONNECT, HTTP Basic to cloud) is observable FAIL evidence; PASS rests on absence, and encrypted M2M is invisible.
assumptions: credential field holds a password, not a token or PSK
group_note: Only cleartext M2M logins observable; encrypted M2M authentication and IXIT review impossible.

summary: Assess documented security guarantees, mechanism fitness, best-practice status and known attacks for authentication cryptography.

units.note: Judge adequacy of claimed security guarantees.
Compare documented crypto details to a reference catalogue.
Check documented crypto against cryptanalytic literature.

rationale: Per v2 conceptual-crypto rule: observed TLS versions/suites judged against TR 103 621 or SOGIS can show non-best-practice (units c, d); units a, b and PASS need IXIT.
assumptions: observed TLS parameters represent the documented authentication cryptography
observed channels cover all authentication mechanisms
group_note: Security-guarantee and holistic mechanism assessment impossible; only observed handshake parameters usable.

summary: Check that the authentication cryptography actually used matches the documented cryptographic details.

units.note: Sniff handshakes/certificates and compare with IXIT; downgrade attempts optional.

rationale: Verdict is deviation of used crypto from IXIT (unit a); per v2.1 not reachable. Catalogue-based judgement of observed TLS is captured in 5.1-3-1.
outside_procedure_cues: TLS versions, cipher suites and certificates of authentication channels are visible in handshakes (TLS 1.3 certificates encrypted).
group_note: Security-guarantee and holistic mechanism assessment impossible; only observed handshake parameters usable.

summary: Assess whether user authentication values can be changed and whether user information explains how, plainly.

units.note: Check documented changeability of authentication factors.
Judge user guidance on changing values; public manual may help.

rationale: Substitution: a public manual explaining value changes can support PASS for units a, b; missing public text cannot show FAIL since guidance may be in the app.
assumptions: published manual covers every user authentication mechanism
group_note: Changing authentication values needs DUT interaction; entire group not passive.

summary: Perform the documented change of user authentication values and verify old values fail and new ones work.
rationale: Units a, b require operating the DUT.
group_note: Changing authentication values needs DUT interaction; entire group not passive.

summary: Assess whether documented brute-force countermeasures on network-addressable authentication make attacks impracticable.
rationale: Unit a is IXIT review only.
outside_procedure_cues: Repeated third-party login attempts reaching the device and its continued responses could hint at missing rate limiting; opportunistic and not used by the TS.
group_note: Brute-force testing is active; only undocumented-mechanism discovery has a passive indication.

summary: Discover undocumented network authentication mechanisms and attempt brute force against documented ones.

units.note: Find network auth mechanisms (scanners/sniffers) not in IXIT.
Attempt brute force against each mechanism.

rationale: Verdict compares discovered network authentication with IXIT (a) and needs brute-force attempts (b); per v2.1 not reachable passively.
outside_procedure_cues: Answering Telnet/HTTP admin/API services expose network authentication; third-party login floods could hint at rate-limit behaviour.
group_note: Brute-force testing is active; only undocumented-mechanism discovery has a passive indication.

summary: Assess whether the vulnerability disclosure policy is accessible to anyone without accounts or similar barriers.

units.note: Check open access to the published VDP, e.g. vendor website.

rationale: Substitution: unit a judged from the openly reachable vendor VDP; PASS reachable, FAIL would rest on not finding it.
assumptions: publicly found VDP is the publication the IXIT designates
group_note: Only checks needing IXIT location of VDP; public lookup covers the substance.

summary: Verify the VDP is public and contains contact details plus acknowledgement and status-update timelines.

units.note: Check VDP content for contact and timelines.

rationale: Units a, b are decidable from the published VDP; failing to find it is absence and needs care.
group_note: Only checks needing IXIT location of VDP; public lookup covers the substance.

summary: Assess whether documented actions and time frames ensure timely handling of disclosed vulnerabilities, plus SO confirmation.

units.note: Judge actions/time frames per vulnerability type.

rationale: Units a, b depend on SO process documentation.
outside_procedure_cues: Public advisory and CVE dates compared with observed firmware updates could indicate handling speed; the TS case reviews only IXIT.
group_note: Internal vulnerability handling process; nothing passive.

summary: Assess documented processes for monitoring, identifying and rectifying vulnerabilities, plus SO confirmation.
rationale: Units a-d review internal manufacturer processes.
group_note: Internal monitoring process; nothing passive.

summary: Assess justifications for non-updatable components and apply the update-mechanism design review of 5.3-2-1.
rationale: Units a, b are IXIT reviews; component inventory is internal.
outside_procedure_cues: Observed update traffic shows some components are updatable; the conceptual case cannot use it.
group_note: Justification of non-updatable components impossible; misuse only indicated by insecure update transport.

summary: Apply the functional update-misuse attacks of 5.3-2-2 to each referenced update mechanism.
rationale: Unit a is attack-based; passively, plaintext or unexpected-source update downloads indicate misuse potential, but on-device verification must be assumed.
assumptions: device does not verify update authenticity itself
group_note: Justification of non-updatable components impossible; misuse only indicated by insecure update transport.

summary: Assess whether the documented design of each update mechanism prevents attacker misuse.

units.note: Review guarantees, description, crypto and initiation of each mechanism.

rationale: Unit a is IXIT design review.
outside_procedure_cues: Firmware fetched over plaintext HTTP or from unexpected hosts bears on misuse resistance; the design review gives no way to use it.
group_note: Design review and actual misuse attacks impossible; insecure update transport is only an indication.

summary: Devise and execute attacks (MITM, rollback, tampered packages) to test whether update misuse is prevented.
rationale: Units a, b are active; NET-OBS only indicates exposure (e.g. firmware over HTTP) without showing the DUT would accept a manipulated update.
assumptions: device does not verify update authenticity itself
group_note: Design review and actual misuse attacks impossible; insecure update transport is only an indication.

summary: Assess whether each software component has at least one update mechanism simple for users to apply.
rationale: Unit a is IXIT review; unattended update traffic is not part of the TS method.
outside_procedure_cues: Update downloads without visible user activity would suggest automatic application, i.e. simple updating; only a conceptual case exists.
group_note: Group has only a conceptual case; passive update observations cannot be used by the TS method.

summary: Assess from IXIT whether at least one update mechanism can be configured to run automatically.
rationale: Unit a is IXIT review.
outside_procedure_cues: Unattended update traffic suggests an automated mechanism; the conceptual case cannot use it.
group_note: Configuration options not visible; automatic behaviour only inferred from unattended update traffic.

summary: Check in the DUT configuration that at least one update mechanism can be automated.

units.note: Inspect DUT settings for automation option.

rationale: Unit a needs settings; observed update downloads without user action suggest automation, but user-triggered updates cannot be excluded passively.
group_note: Configuration options not visible; automatic behaviour only inferred from unattended update traffic.

summary: Identify automatic update mechanisms and check that consent to enable them is queried and honoured at initialisation.
rationale: Units a-c are IXIT reviews.
group_note: Consent query during initialisation requires DUT interaction; nothing passive.

summary: During setup, verify consent is requested and the automatic update state follows the user's choice.
rationale: Units a-c require running initialisation and choosing consent; traffic alone cannot link update behaviour to the user's choice.
group_note: Consent query during initialisation requires DUT interaction; nothing passive.

summary: Assess from IXIT whether update mechanisms check for security updates during or after initialisation.
rationale: Unit a is IXIT review; periodic update-check traffic is not used by the TS.
outside_procedure_cues: Periodic requests to update endpoints after setup would show update checking; the provision has only a conceptual case, so this evidence is unused.
group_note: Only conceptual case exists; periodic update-check traffic is not used by the TS method.

summary: For automatic update mechanisms, check documented user ability to enable, disable and postpone them.
rationale: Units a, b are IXIT reviews.
group_note: User configuration options require UI access.

summary: Verify in the DUT configuration that users can enable, disable and postpone automatic updates.
rationale: Unit a requires UI access.
group_note: User configuration options require UI access.

summary: For mechanisms with update notifications, check documented user ability to enable and disable them.
rationale: Unit a is IXIT review.
group_note: Notification settings require UI access.

summary: Verify in the DUT configuration that users can enable and disable update notifications.
rationale: Unit a requires UI access.
group_note: Notification settings require UI access.

summary: Assess documented guarantees, fitness, best-practice status and known attacks for update cryptography.
rationale: Per v2 conceptual-crypto rule: TLS versions/suites seen on update connections judged against TR 103 621 or SOGIS can show non-best-practice (c, d); signatures and units a, b need IXIT.
assumptions: observed update-channel TLS represents the documented update cryptography
package signature crypto is not judged
group_note: Update crypto review is IXIT-based; observed update-channel TLS is not what the TS assesses.

summary: Assess whether documented security-update procedures and time frames enable timely deployment, plus confirmation.
rationale: Units a, b are internal process documentation.
outside_procedure_cues: Gap between public vulnerability disclosure and observed firmware update arrival could indicate timeliness; the case reviews only procedures.
group_note: Manufacturer procedures and time frames are internal.

summary: Assess whether updates are checked for authenticity and integrity, and whether the DUT itself performs the checks.
rationale: Units a-d review IXIT; on-device verification is internal.
group_note: On-device verification is internal; nothing passive.

summary: Mixed case: review update verification via a trust relationship and discover undocumented network update mechanisms.

units.note: Judge trust relationship for network updates.
Find network update paths not in IXIT via traffic analysis.

rationale: TS labels it conceptual/functional. Bullets on verification and trust relationship review IXIT design (a, b); unit c compares discovered update paths with IXIT; per v2.1 none reachable.
outside_procedure_cues: Update checks and downloads over plaintext HTTP or from unexpected hosts show network update paths and unauthenticated channels; signature use stays unknown.
group_note: Trust-relationship design review impossible; only discovery of undocumented network update paths is passive.

summary: Assess whether users are informed recognisably about required security updates, including risks mitigated.
rationale: Units a, b are IXIT reviews of user notifications.
group_note: User notification content requires UI/IXIT.

summary: Check whether users are notified when an update will disrupt basic functioning.
rationale: Unit a is IXIT review.
group_note: Disruption notifications require UI/IXIT.

summary: Assess whether the published support period can be found and understood by a non-expert user.

units.note: Judge findability/clarity of published support period.

rationale: Substitution: unit a judged from the vendor's public support-period page; findable and clear gives PASS, findable but unclear gives FAIL; not finding it proves nothing.
assumptions: publicly found page is the publication the IXIT designates
model inferred from network identity is correct
group_note: Checking access route as described in IXIT and IXIT support period remains impossible.

summary: Verify the access route to the support period works as documented, is unrestricted, and actually defines the period.

units.note: Check published period matches IXIT support period.

rationale: Unit b and publication existence decidable from PUBLIC; units a, c compare with IXIT and remain open.
group_note: Checking access route as described in IXIT and IXIT support period remains impossible.

summary: Checks that the published explanation of why a device receives no updates, and how hardware replacement is supported, is clear to non-experts.

units.note: Judge clarity of published rationale and replacement info.

rationale: Substitution: unit a judged from public rationale and replacement pages; clarity decides PASS or FAIL once found. Applicability (not updatable) cannot be shown passively.
assumptions: publicly found pages are the publications the IXIT designates
group_note: IXIT-described access route impossible; condition itself not passively decidable.

summary: Verify access to rationale and replacement plan works as documented, is unrestricted, and covers period and method.
rationale: Units b-d decidable from PUBLIC; unit a needs IXIT.
group_note: IXIT-described access route impossible; condition itself not passively decidable.

summary: Assess whether the documented isolation method can remove the DUT from its network or place it in a closed environment.
rationale: Unit a is IXIT review.
group_note: Isolation must be performed on the DUT.

summary: Isolate the DUT as documented and check that only connectivity-related functions are lost.
rationale: Units a-c require performing isolation and checking device function; reconnect loops after outages say nothing about main function.
outside_procedure_cues: During internet outages traffic shows reconnect behaviour, but not whether the main function survives.
group_note: Isolation must be performed on the DUT.

summary: Assess whether the documented hardware replacement method is suitable.
rationale: Unit a is IXIT review.
group_note: Hardware replacement must be performed physically.

summary: Replace the hardware as documented and verify connectivity and functions are regained.
rationale: Units a, b need physical action.
group_note: Hardware replacement must be performed physically.

summary: Assess whether the model designation is clearly recognisable by label or user interface.
rationale: Unit a concerns label or UI; network-advertised model names are not label/UI.
outside_procedure_cues: SSDP/mDNS model names reveal a network-advertised model, which is not the label/UI the provision requires.
group_note: Label/UI inspection needs physical or UI access.

summary: Obtain the model designation as documented and check it is plain text and matches IXIT.
rationale: Units a, b require physical/UI access and IXIT.
group_note: Label/UI inspection needs physical or UI access.

summary: Assess consistency of SSP types, adequacy of guarantees and protection schemes, and completeness of the SSP list.
rationale: Units a-d are IXIT reviews.
group_note: Storage protection is internal.

summary: Check that documented storage protection schemes for SSPs are actually implemented.

units.note: Probe storage protection, e.g. unprivileged access attempts.

rationale: Unit a requires internal access or active probing.
group_note: Storage protection is internal.

summary: Check hard-coded identities are declared and that their documented protection provides tamper resistance.
rationale: Units a-c are IXIT reviews; identifiers seen on the wire cannot be shown to be hard-coded security identities.
group_note: Tamper resistance is internal/physical.

summary: Check that tamper-resistance protection of hard-coded identities is implemented as documented.
rationale: Unit a is physical/internal inspection.
group_note: Tamper resistance is internal/physical.

summary: Check hard-coded CSPs are documented and that their provisioning prevents their use in operation.

units.note: Check documented hard-coding reflected in description.

rationale: Units a, b are IXIT reviews; public hard-coded-credential CVEs are not part of the TS method.
outside_procedure_cues: Identical credentials across same-model devices, or a public CVE on hard-coded keys for the identified model, would indicate hard-coded CSPs.
group_note: Source code and provisioning internal; public hard-coded-credential CVEs are outside the TS method.

summary: Check that the documented provisioning replacing hard-coded CSPs is really applied during operation.

units.note: Observe provisioning, e.g. user prompted for individual data.

rationale: Unit a needs operating setup; traffic cannot reveal that a credential is hard-coded.
group_note: Source code and provisioning internal; public hard-coded-credential CVEs are outside the TS method.

summary: Check CSPs for update verification and service communication are documented and generated unique per device with sound mechanisms.

units.note: Judge generation mechanism using public standards.

rationale: Unit a is IXIT only; unit b judges IXIT generation description, public catalogues are only aids.
outside_procedure_cues: The same client certificate or credential seen on several devices of one model would suggest non-unique CSPs.
group_note: Generation mechanisms are documented only in IXIT.
